title: CRM Implementation Services, Process and Cost | Stacktik
metaDescription: CRM implementation by Stacktik: the CRM chosen, set up and connected to calling and outreach, your data migrated, your team trained. Fixed fee in writing.
h1: CRM implementation for sales teams, from first call to handover.
lede: CRM implementation is the work of putting a customer relationship management (CRM) system into daily use: choosing the system, setting it up around how your team sells, moving your data in, connecting calling, outreach and reporting to it, and training the people who use it. Stacktik, a RevOps (revenue operations) consultancy in Woodbridge, Ontario, runs CRM implementation as a scoped project for a fixed fee, quoted in writing before work starts.

summary.label: What it is
summary.text: CRM implementation is choosing a CRM, setting it up, migrating your data, connecting calling, outreach and reporting to it, and training your team to use it.

summary.label: Who it is for
summary.text: Sales and customer-facing teams choosing a first sales CRM, replacing one, or fixing a CRM that was bought but never set up properly.

summary.label: What you get
summary.text: A CRM configured in your own account, your data moved in, your other tools connected, recorded training sessions and written handover notes.

summary.label: How it is priced
summary.text: A fixed fee for the implementation, quoted in writing before work starts. Software stays on the vendor's own plan and pricing. The first call is free.

blocks.h2: What CRM implementation covers, from setup to CRM integration.
blocks.intro: A sales CRM is the system where every customer, opportunity and conversation lives, and the one your other tools connect to. Every Stacktik project is scoped on a written proposal, so the list below is what we draw from, not a fixed package.

items.title: CRM setup
items.body: Pipeline stages, with written rules for when an opportunity moves forward. Lead routing in turn, by territory, or to whoever is on duty. We start from how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team.

items.title: CRM data migration
items.body: Your records are moved from your current system or from spreadsheets, and duplicates are merged. The old system stays read-only during the switch. After that it is yours to close.

items.title: CRM integration
items.body: The phone system is connected to the CRM, so calls are logged on the record with the recording. Email sequences run with rules that stop them. Reports pull from the CRM, the phone system and the outreach tool.

items.title: Automation and AI agents
items.body: Automations between tools, documented. AI agents built on Claude or OpenAI take routine steps: call notes written to the record, inbound leads qualified, follow-ups drafted for a rep to approve.

items.title: Training on your own data
items.body: Training sessions use your own data and are recorded for the team. Handover notes say how each piece runs and who to call about it.

items.title: A revenue scoreboard
items.body: Targets per rep and per team, a live leaderboard, and the reports the owner reads, pulled from the CRM and the phone system and updating without anyone typing.

blocks.h2: The CRM implementation process, step by step.
blocks.intro: At Stacktik, the written proposal is your CRM implementation plan. It lists the steps for your project, their order and what we need from your team. One technical RevOps consultant is assigned to your project and stays with it from the first idea to fully deployed.

items.title: A free first call
items.body: We go through what you use today, what isn't working, and whether the next step is software, implementation, both, or nothing yet. There is no obligation.

items.title: A shortlist and a written proposal
items.body: We map how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team, then shortlist two or three CRMs with the monthly cost of each. The proposal sets out the scope, the fixed fee and what counts as done.

items.title: CRM setup in your account
items.body: The subscription is in your name, bought through our partner programs or direct from the vendor. You create a named admin seat for us, and we build the pipeline stages and lead routing inside your account.

items.title: Your data moved over
items.body: Records come across from your current system or spreadsheets, and duplicates are merged. The old system is read-only during the switch, then yours to close.

items.title: Calling, outreach and reporting connected
items.body: The phone system is connected so calls log to the record with the recording. Email sequences stop when a reply comes in. Automations between tools are documented, and reports pull from every system.

items.title: Training and handover
items.body: Your team is trained on the setup, on their own data, and the sessions are recorded. Handover notes say how each piece runs and who to call. You revoke our admin seat. Monthly support afterwards is optional.

blocks.intro: There are two separate numbers, both on the Stacktik proposal: what the software costs you each month, and what our work costs. There are no prices on this page because every job is scoped. These are the things that move each number.

items.title: Plan and seat count
items.body: The software is on the vendor's own plan and pricing. The monthly figure depends on the plan and the number of seats. Where a vendor program provides a customer offer, it is applied and shown on the proposal, whether or not we do your setup.

items.title: How much data moves
items.body: Moving records out of one current system is a different job from pulling them out of several spreadsheets. What is moved, and from where, is part of the scope on the proposal.

items.title: How many tools connect
items.body: A CRM on its own is a smaller project than a CRM with a phone system, an outreach tool and a reporting dashboard connected to it. The tools to connect are part of the scope on the proposal.

items.title: Automation, AI agents and custom tools
items.body: Automations between tools, AI agents for routine steps, and any internal tool or connector we build where no platform covers a step are scoped and quoted on the same proposal.

items.title: Additions and ongoing support
items.body: The proposal says what is in scope, what is not, and what an addition would cost. Support after handover is optional and monthly, with its own scope and fee.

blocks.h2: How to choose a CRM implementation consultant or partner.
blocks.intro: CRM consulting ranges from one vendor's own onboarding to a full build across several tools. These are the points worth checking with any CRM consultant before you sign, and how Stacktik answers each one.

items.title: Scope and fee in writing
items.body: Ask for the scope, what is out of scope, the fee and what counts as done before work starts. Stacktik quotes implementation as a fixed fee in writing, with what an addition would cost.

items.title: One named person on the work
items.body: Ask who builds it. At Stacktik a technical RevOps consultant is assigned to your project: the same person on the call, the proposal and the build, from the first idea to fully deployed.

items.title: Vendor relationships disclosed
items.body: Ask whether the vendor pays the consultant. Stacktik is enrolled in vendor partner programs with most of the platforms it sets up, and the proposal states its relationship with each one next to its price.

items.title: Software and setup kept separate
items.body: A consultant should not tie the two together. With Stacktik you can buy direct and hire us only for the implementation, or buy through us and run the setup yourself.

items.title: Work across every tool
items.body: The CRM is the system your other tools connect to. Check that the consultant sets up calling, outreach and reporting across every tool, not one vendor's. If the vendor's own onboarding is enough for your case, we say so.

items.title: Limits stated up front
items.body: Ask what the consultant does not do. Stacktik does not usually take on Salesforce or ERP migrations, write your email copy, or run your outbound for you. We build it; your team sends it.

platforms.intro: For teams choosing a CRM in Canada, these are the ones Stacktik works with. We are enrolled in vendor partner programs with most platforms we set up, and the proposal states our relationship with each next to its price.

faq.a: The cost of a CRM implementation has two parts: the software, on the vendor's own plan and pricing, and the implementation work. Stacktik quotes the work as a fixed fee, in writing, before it starts, with what is in scope, what is not and what an addition would cost. Every job is scoped, so there are no prices on this page. Nothing is charged for the first call.

faq.q: What are the steps in a CRM implementation plan?
faq.a: At Stacktik, the steps in implementing a CRM are a first call, a shortlist and written proposal, then the work the proposal scopes: setup in your account, data migration, connecting calling, outreach and reporting, training and handover. The proposal lists the steps for your project, their order and what we need from your team, so you see the whole plan before you commit to anything.

faq.q: How do I choose a CRM implementation consultant?
faq.a: Choose a consultant who puts the scope, the fee and what counts as done in writing before work starts. Then check who does the build, whether a vendor pays them, whether they connect the tools around the CRM, and whether you can buy the software and the setup separately. Stacktik quotes a fixed fee in writing, assigns one technical RevOps consultant to your project, and states its relationship with each tool next to its price.

faq.q: What is the best CRM for a small business in Canada?
faq.a: There is no single best CRM for every small business in Canada. The right one fits how your team sells, at a monthly cost you see before you commit. Stacktik maps how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team, then shortlists two or three CRMs with the monthly cost of each for your seat count, so you decide on fit and cost, not on demos.

faq.q: How does CRM data migration work when we switch CRMs?
faq.a: In a CRM migration, your records are moved from the current system or from spreadsheets into the new CRM, and duplicates are merged. With Stacktik, the old system stays read-only during the switch and is then yours to close. Salesforce and ERP migrations are not usually in scope. If the system you run on is not one we list, ask on the call.

faq.q: Can Stacktik be our CRM implementation partner if we already bought the CRM?
faq.a: Yes. Stacktik works as your CRM implementation partner whether you bought the CRM direct, bought it through Stacktik, or have not chosen one yet. You can buy direct and hire us only for the implementation, or buy through us and run the setup yourself. If the vendor's own onboarding is enough for your case, we say so.
